questions.question: What Thapsigargin concentration was selected for antiviral experiments, and what cytotoxicity boundary motivated that choice?

options.A: 0.5 µM, because concentrations through 2 µM did not significantly affect viability but higher concentrations were toxic
options.B: 5 µM, because only concentrations below 0.5 µM affected viability
options.C: 0.05 µM, because all concentrations above 0.1 µM were toxic
options.D: 2 µM, because this was the lowest concentration that reduced viability

questions.rationale: The MTT assay found no significant cytotoxicity from 0.00064 to 2 µM, but toxicity above 2 µM; the authors used 0.5 µM.
questions.evidence_quote: Thapsigargin at concentrations from 0.00064 µM to 2 µM did not significantly affect the cell viability

questions.question: Which virus pattern was observed when cells were treated with 0.5 µM Thapsigargin?

options.A: NDV, PPRV and BHV-1 were inhibited, but BPXV was not
options.B: Only NDV and PPRV were inhibited; both DNA viruses were unaffected
options.C: All four viruses were inhibited equally
options.D: BHV-1 and BPXV were inhibited, but the paramyxoviruses were unaffected

questions.rationale: The study reports significant inhibition of the two paramyxoviruses and BHV-1, but not BPXV.
questions.evidence_quote: It also significantly inhibited BHV-1 (Fig. 1e ) but not BPXV (Fig. 1f ) replication

questions.question: How did the authors distinguish a cellular antiviral effect from direct inactivation of free virions?

options.A: Incubated virions with 0.5 or 5 µM inhibitor for 1.5 h and found no virucidal effect
options.B: Preincubated cells with inhibitor for 96 h and measured viral RNA
options.C: Compared cell-free virions at 0.5 µM with virions inside SERCA2-overexpressing cells
options.D: Used plaque assay only after heating virus suspensions to 37°C for 24 h

questions.rationale: Cell-free virions were exposed to the two drug concentrations before residual infectivity was tested; the treatment did not directly inactivate virus.
questions.evidence_quote: we incubated the infectious virions with either 0.5 µM or 5 µm Thapsigargin for 1.5 h and subsequently tested the residual infectivity

questions.question: What result from SERCA2 overexpression supported a host-factor role for SERCA?

options.A: It facilitated NDV/PPRV replication and rescued the inhibitory effect of Thapsigargin
options.B: It suppressed replication further and increased Thapsigargin toxicity
options.C: It rescued NDV but not PPRV and had no effect on inhibitor response
options.D: It increased cell viability but did not alter viral titers

questions.rationale: Overexpression of SERCA2 both supported viral replication and counteracted the inhibitor's effect.
questions.evidence_quote: overexpression of SERCA2 not only facilitated NDV/PPRV replication, but also rescued the inhibitory effect of Thapsigargin on virus replication

questions.question: When was the strongest inhibition observed in the time-of-addition experiments, and how did later addition affect it?

options.A: When added 30 min before infection; inhibition declined with later addition
options.B: When added 10 h after infection; inhibition increased toward budding
options.C: When added 24 h after infection; only PPRV was affected
options.D: At any time after infection; the magnitude was constant

questions.rationale: For both viruses the inhibitor was most effective before infection, with inhibition diminishing as addition was delayed.
questions.evidence_quote: The highest inhibition was observed when the inhibitor was applied 30 min before infection.

questions.question: Which viral life-cycle stages were not detectably affected in the step-specific assays?
questions.rationale: The authors report no effect on attachment, RNA synthesis or budding, while evidence supported entry and protein-localization defects.
questions.evidence_quote: Thapsigargin was not found to affect virus attachment, RNA synthesis and budding

questions.question: What localization phenotype followed Thapsigargin treatment of infected cells?

options.A: Viral proteins accumulated in cytoplasmic foci in about 70% of treated cells, versus 10–30% of controls
options.B: Viral proteins reached the cell surface in about 70% of treated cells, versus 10–30% of controls
options.C: SERCA and viral proteins perfectly colocalized in all treated cells
options.D: Nuclear viral-protein localization increased while cytoplasmic staining disappeared

questions.rationale: Treated cells predominantly showed defective cytoplasmic-foci localization, while control cells more often showed cell-surface localization.
questions.evidence_quote: Thapsigargin treatment showed defective localization in ~70% of the cells, as compared to DMSO control wherein this proportion was 10-30 %

questions.question: What did 70 passages under Thapsigargin selection reveal about NDV resistance?

options.A: Resistance emerged around P25, was significant by P35, and remained incomplete through P70
options.B: Complete resistance appeared by P25 and remained stable through P70
options.C: No resistance emerged in NDV, but PPRV became fully resistant
options.D: Resistance appeared only in DMSO-passaged controls by P70

questions.rationale: NDV showed a substantial but incomplete loss of sensitivity beginning around passage 25 and significant by passage 35.
questions.evidence_quote: resistance began appearing at ~P25 and significant resistance was observed at P35 (~100 fold-inhibition compared to ~10,000 fold inhibition at zero passage)

questions.question: How did PPRV compare with NDV after long-term passage in the presence of Thapsigargin?

options.A: PPRV retained similar sensitivity through passage 70, unlike the partial NDV resistance
options.B: PPRV became fully resistant while NDV remained fully sensitive
options.C: PPRV showed resistance only under vehicle passage, whereas NDV did not
options.D: Both viruses acquired complete resistance by passage 35

questions.rationale: PPRV samples at P0 and P70 showed similar sensitivity, indicating no comparable resistance acquisition.
questions.evidence_quote: all PPRVs (P0, P70-Thapsigargin and P70-Control) revealed similar sensitivity to Thapsigargin even at passage level 70

questions.question: Which mechanistic question remained unresolved because of experimental limitations?

options.A: The study could not determine direct SERCA–viral-protein interaction; colocalization was imperfect and co-immunoprecipitation failed
options.B: The study could not establish whether Thapsigargin inhibited entry because no entry assay was performed
options.C: The study could not test SERCA2 rescue because only empty-vector cells were used
options.D: The study could not determine whether NDV resistance arose because no long-term passage was done

questions.rationale: The authors explicitly note imperfect colocalization and unsuccessful co-immunoprecipitation, precluding a direct interaction conclusion.
questions.evidence_quote: in this study, we could not determine any direct interaction between SERCA and viral proteins.
